speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) launched the refreshed Built Environment Industry Transformation Map, or ITM, last September.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: CORENET X is a key initiative to support our digitalisation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: CORENET X is a one-stop digital shopfront for the industry to make regulatory submissions for building works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We expect it to bring about significant benefits for both the industry and the agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, CORENET X will drive greater industry collaboration through data interoperability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We will require eligible projects to prepare their plans in Building Information Modelling, or BIM format, which is essentially a 3D digital building model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Consultants will be required to submit their BIM models for these projects through a standard submission format, which is aligned to common data standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will allow for BIM models to be read by various BIM-based software used by other project stakeholders and will also allow consultants across multiple disciplines to coordinate on a single BIM submission.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Data interoperability can also allow contractors and facilities managers to weigh in on the building design at an earlier stage, so that consultants can incorporate considerations for construction and maintenance upfront.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The BIM models can then be passed on to contractors to guide construction downstream and minimise abortive work from creating their own models from scratch.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The capturing of accurate building design data within the BIM models will also facilitate new possibilities, including their use as "digital twins" for building maintenance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Second, the use of new technologies under CORENET X will deliver productivity gains for both the industry and agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: One example is the Collaboration Platform, which will allow Government agencies to review regulatory submissions concurrently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will facilitate collaboration across agencies to put together a clear, consolidated response to consultants, which will help to reduce the number of iterations between agencies and the industry today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We intend to introduce an Automated Model Checker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will automate the checking of regulatory rules and speed up compliance checks for agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The industry can also utilise the checker to review their designs and correct any non-compliances before making their submissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Third, CORENET X will support a redesigned process for regulatory submissions for building works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Today, the project team submits different sets of building plans across various touchpoints for different agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This can result in discrepancies leading to plan adjustments and abortive work, which can delay the completion timeline for projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: There will also be an optional Piling Gateway between the Design and Construction Gateways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will provide flexibility for projects to start piling work earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: At each submission gateway, agencies will provide a consolidated response to each submission from the industry, rather than issuing piecemeal directions in silos.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This coordinated process will enable cross-agency issues and conflicts to be identified and resolved in a systemic manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, taken together, CORENET X can help reduce the overall time and effort from the industry to obtain approvals across the development process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For smaller projects, agencies have also streamlined requirements to expedite regulatory approvals under CORENET X.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, simpler works, such as minor standalone structures, can enjoy a Direct Submission Process, or DSP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Under DSP, such works will only require a single submission, compared to the submissions at the Design and Construction Gateways required for other works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It will also harmonise regulatory processes across agencies, in tandem with CORENET X.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, when applying for Written Permission, or WP, Qualified Persons (QP) must submit a full set of design details complying with Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA)'s guidelines and requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Where there are non-compliances, URA may issue Provisional Permission, or PP, instead of WP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This means that QPs will only be required to submit key design parameters to receive the PP earlier at the Design Gateway, together with similar clearances from other agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The design can then be developed in greater detail to be submitted for URA's approval of the WP later on, at the Construction Gateway.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This new process will help QPs to avoid reworking detailed designs at a later stage, because issues with key design parameters would be picked up by regulators earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Today, agencies already allow for the lodgment of building plans for simple submissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Under the lodgment process, QPs declare that their building plans are compliant with agencies' requirements, and approvals are expedited.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Third, amendments to regularise approvals under EPMA and EPHA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Today, NEA ensures that building plans comply with pollution control and environmental public health requirements by administratively riding on BCA's approvals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clauses 16 to 18 and 20 will amend the EPMA and EPHA to provide the Director-General of Environmental Protection and the Director-General of Public Health with powers to ensure that building and other works meet pollution control requirements and environmental public health requirements respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This involves providing them with powers to grant approvals for controlled works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Both Director-Generals will also have powers of enforcement, such as by issuing directions and imposing timelines for project parties to comply with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Fourth, amendments to enable electronic service of relevant documents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Without the close partnership and valuable insights of industry stakeholders, it would not have been possible for us to bring CORENET X to fruition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Since 2018, more than 100 industry representatives have worked with us to develop the new CORENET X regulatory approval process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Agencies have also established Communities of Practice with various industry stakeholders, including consultants and developers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This involves monthly meetings for agencies to provide progress updates and receive feedback on the development of CORENET X.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We are also working with the industry on sandbox projects to test out and refine the new features and processes prior to launch.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The sandbox involves submissions from both public and private sector projects across various building typologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This iterative process of seeking inputs and incorporating feedback has built a deep vein of trust and understanding between agencies and the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As we roll out CORENET X in the coming years, we will leverage this close partnership to ensure its success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As with any new system, we recognise that all parties will require sufficient time to adjust to the changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To this end, we will onboard users in phases and roll out features progressively, beginning with a soft launch of CORENET X in December this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As a start, we will work with partner firms to test out the new features, with projects of varying sizes and building typologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For the first year following the launch, we will gradually encourage more submissions for new projects to come on board on a voluntary basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will encourage the industry to familiarise themselves with the new platform and processes and ensure a smooth transition as we move towards onboarding all submissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This phased approach will provide the industry with sufficient time to prepare for CORENET X.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We have put in place various resources, such as training courses, industry briefings and webinars, a Code of Practice as a guide for submission requirements and a dedicated CORENET X website with self-help resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: And we will continue to work closely with trade associations and professional boards to reach out to their members, including smaller firms, to inform and train them on the use of CORENET X.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To date, we have trained more than 350 industry professionals on the submission requirements and the new regulatory approval process under CORENET X.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: An example of an SME firm that has upskilled itself is DCA Architects, which has adapted its inhouse workflows to align with the new CORENET X processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: DCA Architects is also preparing its project team for CORENET X submissions by participating in the CORENET X sandbox and is sending its QPs for the necessary training programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Local SMEs will now be able to receive up to 50% funding support for qualifying solutions, to help them make the transition to BIM under CORENET X.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: BCA will release more details in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We will pay close attention to the industry readiness for CORENET X through regular checks with the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In the meantime, I encourage our industry practitioners, especially QPs, to tap on the various resources available and upskill yourselves to reap the full benefits of CORENET X.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, please do approach BCA or your respective trade associations for more details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: CORENET X will create productivity savings and reduce regulatory burden for both the industry and agencies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I commend the Government agencies and the industry for their collaborative approach in creating the new CORENET X platform.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The platform streamlines our planning process into a single submission by developers and a coordinated response across agencies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a good example of how all stakeholders can work together for better outcomes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three points of clarification on the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification is on safeguards for preliminary approvals.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand it is important to give developers flexibility to commence work early while waiting for final permission.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, once preliminary work has begun, it becomes harder to change course.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would it be difficult for the agencies to refuse final permission, knowing that developers have already incurred expenses?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What if rectification costs are too high or not even possible and the damage is already done?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify what safeguards will be taken when giving provisional or preliminary permission to minimise such risks?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second clarification is on the scope of defences under the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under section 20 of the BCA, the new subsection 1 states that it is a defence to lodging a non-compliant plan if the accused reasonably believed the plans complied with all the prescribed regulations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Similarly, in the new section 33H of the EPMA, it is an offence to deviate "in a material way" from the plans under a clearance certificate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What is the threshold for the deviation to be considered material?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Providing guidance and examples on how these terms are applied would be useful for developers to know the extent of due diligence expected.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have raised this a number of times in this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These updates to planning permissions are commendable but we still have not taken the critical step of introducing a formal EIA law.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: EIA is an essential exercise to ensure that we properly balance the benefits of development to the costs to our environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Loss of natural spaces and biodiversity adversely affects the lives of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We not only are denied the enjoyment of natural spaces, we also lose an invaluable resource for combating climate change.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Minister for National Development has previously stated that even though we have no formal EIA laws, the EIA framework is built into the planning approvals and agencies can require an EIA to be undertaken.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also recognise that we are taking steps to centralise EIA requirements under NParks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A law to mandate EIA has several benefits over the current case-by-case approach.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Developers would know the cost of falling short.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They would be able to plan ahead of time and not need to await some government decision.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Agencies would not need to make as many case-by-case assessments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singaporeans could be consulted to ensure the law reflects their values and priorities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The law could also contain principles and rules to standardise when and how information gets disclosed, strengthening our Government's principle of transparency.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Senior Minister of State can consider these benefits and periodically review our planning framework to consider codifying an EIA law.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Beyond these improvements to regulatory frameworks and while I acknowledge that many steps have been taken in this direction, I urge the Government to apply even greater efforts towards minimising work safety incidents in the construction industry.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Workplace fatalities have been on the rise, following the winding down of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Most recently, a 20-year-old migrant worker was killed due to the collapse of a concrete wall at a work site in Tanjong Pagar.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Earlier this year, there was a construction worker who fell from a roof while doing waterproofing work and a migrant worker who was killed by falling bars.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The project Migrant Death Map, a volunteer-driven initiative, documented all migrant worker deaths from January 2000 to mid-2022 and investigated the key issues surrounding these deaths.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The project found that the lack of safety at work sites and migrant workers' work practices were not inherent to the nature of the work as many accidents were preventable and involved employer negligence, which may be symptomatic of prioritising financial gain over labour safety.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Apart from the safety infrastructure, worker's healthcare, mental health and transportation facilities all play a part in creating a safe working environment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The hon Minister for Manpower Tan See Leng reported to the House in July last year that for the past five years, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) received around 2,400 to 3,800 reports a year on unsafe acts in workplaces from various channels such as the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) hotline, eFeedback on MOM's website and referrals from non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and unions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The Minister also mentioned that MOM assesses each element of feedback and aims to ensure that relevant companies make the required rectifications and encourage workers to report unsafe workplace conditions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: While these are welcome measures, the number of workplace fatalities suggest that there is much more to be done.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: These deaths amount to a moral call to action to save lives, but they also underline what is at stake in protecting our national brand and reputation as a caring society.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I have a few suggestions to make for the Ministry's consideration.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Companies can then improve from the failures of themselves and others, thereby enabling the benchmarking of safety procedures.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: While the immediate cause of the accident is investigated and made known through a coroner's inquiry – in the case of a fatality, that is – it is not known whether and how companies explore the deeper reasons behind safety lapses and make the necessary changes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For instance, for the migrant worker who was killed by bars falling on him, the coroner's inquiry found that he had been using an unapproved method of securing the bars, resulting in the wire securing the bundle of bars, which was being lifted by a tower crane, snapping.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Two workers who noticed the mistake on a previous occasion did not highlight the mistake to their supervisor.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It is unclear why they did not do so.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Reasons could include a lack of training, reporting procedure or an inclination to complete the job faster.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Rectification and stop work orders issued by MOM should ensure that companies make swift initial assessments and rectifications, including prompt solutions to safety reporting, when an accident happens, while waiting for the results of an investigation that should provide root cause analysis.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Moreover, safety codes should be made as simple and visual as possible so that workers can fully comprehend the safety procedure.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Awareness-based training tackles the impact of work pressure resulting in the compromise of safety boundaries.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It would be key to follow safety procedures and draw attention to the importance of doing so.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: On an everyday basis, one way could be using the pointing and calling method which we commonly see in Japanese companies, where every safety step taken is loudly stated, verbalised or called out.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This helps to increase focus on the safety measures taken.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: On a more structural level, companies must set up adequate procedures for reporting to ensure that workers understand that safety is crucial.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: While Singapore has similar regulations, the law in Japan requires the committee to circulate an agenda to all employees and provide opportunities to hear workers' opinions on matters related to workplace safety and health.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This ensures that the opinions of the employees are reflected in the safety and health measures undertaken by the employer.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, the Government, of course, needs to regulate construction companies by invoking appropriate punishments to compel companies to ensure a safe working environment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: There is a framework for doing that, and that is done.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: While there is a Safety Disqualification Framework, though, to disqualify contractors with a certain number of demerit points from Public Sector's construction tenders, the demerit points framework has room to be tightened further.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Companies have the leeway to accumulate a few breaches in safety before being disqualified from tenders.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Instead, it is companies that are penalised, without the individuals responsible being punished.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: If workplace accidents are not reduced significantly as a result of the other measures being taken, this should be reviewed.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Apart from looking into major workplace safety concerns, there are also issues of concern with heat, especially with our rising temperatures amidst climate change.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Construction workers are disproportionately affected because they have to wear heavy safety gear like helmets and thick rubber boots, which trap huge amounts of heat.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Migrant workers lack access to cooling technology because they work outdoors and at times in remote areas.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In addition to inspections, we can look more into the way construction sites are built.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: There should be access to shaded areas and access to water facilities and even perhaps access to air-conditioned rest areas, whether from the work site or nearby areas.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: The built environment sector professionals I spoke to look forward to a CORENET X that can bring about improved efficiency and faster approvals.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: They also hope CORENET X can become the digital foundation for the entire sector in the future.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This is a huge undertaking, a critical part of our built environment sector's transformation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Some large architecture firms have been working with our agencies on CORENET X through industry consultations and feedback sessions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: It is likely that MND has factored in their views.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Therefore, I am here to share the feedback of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) architecture companies that use CORENET often, as well as some main contractors who use certain features of CORENET.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: The four key feedbacks I have heard are as follows.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: One, built sector professionals would like to know more about how agencies will come together to approve the key gateways, specifically the Design Gateways, Construction Gateways, as well as the OP/Stat Completion stage.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Today, architects seek approval from agencies, which may take time depending on complexity.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: For example, agencies may take a while to approve a change in the Building Plan when an undocumented gas or water pipe is found in a brownfield development.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Currently, the industry may continue working on the project, even as they are waiting for that one or two agencies' approval at the building plan level.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: For example, from the National Parks Board (NParks) on relocating of trees, the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) on fire safety for the design of a stairwell.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: The question is: in the future, do all agencies need to sign off at a particular gateway before one can commence work?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: What happens when there is an unexpected site condition, which is common in brownfield developments, is discovered and requires a minor amendment?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Will they need to get all the agencies to approve the revised design?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: If so, would getting all agencies to sign off lead to longer delays?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And if not, does the regulatory process differ for 2D and BIM submissions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Most professionals agree that BIM is the future, but not everyone can use it yet.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: For our SMEs, the issue is cost, not technology.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Our SMEs can upgrade their software to do BIM and many professionals have the basic skills, but SMEs need to invest in training and to redesign their processes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: SMEs can also outsource BIM creation to overseas companies in the Philippines or Indonesia.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This cost is justified if they can really benefit from productivity improvements.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Or the cost will simply be passed to the end-user.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: It will be ideal if MND can publicly set a desired timeline, but also adjust the milestones depending on how fast our agencies get fully ready, and for our industry to acquire the capabilities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Three, MND must pay special attention to the CORENET X roll-out to ensure it goes well.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Several years ago, the industry experienced difficulties during the initial roll-out of CORENET 2.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This includes server downtime and issues with Singpass login.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: For CORENET X, given how important it is to the industry, MND should work hard to avoid the same issues.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Using data garnered from CORENET X applications and approvals, agencies can jointly identify solutions to common but complex building designing issues.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: MND will also know if agencies have insufficient staff strength to process approvals, because they now see the data from all agencies, and MND can work with them to close the manpower gap.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Doing so will benefit the built sector tremendously.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: To conclude, there is a proverb: "If you want to go fast, run alone; if you want to go far, run together." This rings true for CORENET X, and I believe MND is committed to co-creating CORENET X with the industry.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Today's debate on the bill is an important step to getting CORENET X ready, and to increasing the built sector's knowledge of it.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Therefore, I hope MND can answer some of the questions that I have raised on behalf of the SMEs within the built sector.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Notwithstanding my questions, I support the amendments to the Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I will start with the points regarding the redesigned regulatory process under CORENET X.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: At each gateway, project teams will need to consolidate the critical project requirements and submit them for approval.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Agencies will then work together to provide a consolidated and coordinated response to project teams.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Project teams can then proceed with the relevant works after each gateway is cleared.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This streamlined process will minimise abortive works later, by ensuring that key parameters associated with each gateway are jointly reviewed by agencies, before works proceed.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, for the specific examples raised by Mr Louis Ng, the design certificates under the Environmental Protection and Management Act or EPMA, and Environmental Public Health Act or EPHA, and the provisional permission under the Planning Act, would only be granted after agencies have jointly assessed that the key environmental and planning parameters for the project are in order at the Design Gateway.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This would give project teams greater assurance to commence some preliminary works, without needing to wait for agencies' approvals of the detailed building design at the Construction Gateway.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Ng also asked about the lodgment scheme under the Building Control Act, or BC Act.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is a business-friendly measure that will provide the industry with expedited approvals for less complex, lower risk building works.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: BCA has observed that the plans submitted by QPs for such works today are usually in order and downstream rectification works are not likely to be required.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That said, the Commissioner of Building Control may still require the plans to be submitted for approval if he or she views that they are not fully compliant.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This provides a safeguard in the event that certain plans will require more detailed review.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked if there would be delays due to the consolidated approvals from agencies at the various gateways.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the contrary, this new process should help project teams save time.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As mentioned, this should reduce abortive works, as agencies would jointly review the plans and resolve any conflicts upfront.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: QPs would no longer need to keep adjusting their plans, to reconcile and address different requirements from different agencies at multiple points of the approval process.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In addition, we will establish service standards to ensure that agencies provide timely responses to project teams at each gateway.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I fully agree with Mr Kwek that CORENET X involves significant changes, both for the agencies and the industry.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Hence, we will need to ensure a smooth transition from the existing CORENET platform.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That is why we have worked with the industry on sandbox projects to test out and refine the new features and processes.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will onboard users in phases and roll out features progressively and make adjustments as necessary.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will first work with partner firms to test out the new features from the soft launch in December 2023, before gradually accepting more submissions on a voluntary basis.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Agencies will also provide helpdesk support as CORENET X is progressively rolled out.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We are also paying special attention to the needs of our SMEs, as mentioned by Mr Kwek.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In particular, we are helping them make the shift from 2D submissions to Building Information Modelling, or BIM, submissions.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We plan to implement this PSG support within the next few months.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I encourage our SMEs to tap on the support available and start your BIM journey as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: First, on the new section 20(1A) of the BC Act.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This provision allows for an accused to argue that they reasonably believed that the plans lodged were compliant with the necessary requirements.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In each case, whether the defence is made out would depend on the specific facts, such as the qualifications and experience of the accused, the nature of the work, and other relevant factors.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Second, on the new section 33H of the EPMA, this provision stipulates that it is an offence to carry out controlled works that deviate in any material way from approved plans.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The intent is to ensure that the works are carried out according to approved plans in order to prevent pollution.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NEA will determine whether to pursue any enforcement action based on the facts of each case.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Whether a deviation is considered material would depend on the circumstances of the case including, but not limited to, prevailing requirements under NEA's codes of practice and legislation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Both BCA and NEA will conduct formal investigations and examine the facts of the case carefully, before embarking on any enforcement action under these provisions.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Third, on the need for Environmental Impact Assessment, or EIA, legislation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is not within the scope of the Bill, but let me briefly clarify nonetheless.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Environmental considerations are already integrated into our planning process.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: If the impact on the environment could be significant, agencies will ask for an environmental study to assess in greater detail the full impact and develop more mitigation measures to minimise the impact of the development.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: EIA reports are also made publicly available online, unless there are reasons to maintain confidentiality, such as security considerations.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is also not within the scope of the Bill but let me briefly respond.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The safety of our workers is a priority for all of us in the built environment sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Mr Perera may not have been in the Chamber when the Parliamentary Question was answered this morning.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is the question raised by Mr Yip Hon Weng.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower Mr Zaqy Mohamad had also given a fairly comprehensive reply to Mr Yip.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Workplace safety is an important priority for us.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: When accidents happen, it is an opportunity for us to reflect, learn and see how we can do better as an industry, as a sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Every fatality is a tragedy that we hope to avoid for future building works.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This culture, this safety mindset is in line with our entire effort to transform the way we build in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Many of the efforts under the refreshed build environment Industry Transformation Map (ITM) would not only raise productivity, but also improve workplace safety and put workers' safety at the centre of what we do.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For instance, using robotics and automation, we reduce both the need for manual labour as well as the safety risk for workers.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Our shift towards pre-fabrication using Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA) technologies will move more construction work from worksites into factory-like settings.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This can lead to better worker safety outcomes, with fewer workers deployed on site.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Agencies will place greater emphasis on safety considerations in tender requirements and evaluations.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Agencies also intend to implement sector-specific measures, such as improving the training for our workers, to improve safety outcomes.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, many of the suggestions raised by Mr Leon Perera – and I thank him for those suggestions – had also been considered by the MAST task force and we will continue to see how we can improve and incorporate good practices, not just from overseas but good practices within our firms in our sector, and share these good practices with many of our industry partners.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And when an accident or incident occurs, how will we get learning points from that incident after our investigation and see how we can do better as a community to support our migrant workers here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, those suggestions around demerit points, safety committees, in-depth sharing of knowledge and best practices, these are things we will continue to look at.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That said, firms must also take ownership and see worker safety as a core part of their operations.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Individuals must also take responsibility for keeping themselves and their fellow workers at the worksite safe.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Together, we can do our part to look after our migrant workers and ensure their safety.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: CORENET X is, indeed, a significant milestone for our built environment sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We have been partnering the sector closely during its conceptualisation and development and we will continue to work with the sector to take in feedback and help firms prepare for the shift to CORENET X.
